title: [PowerRename] "Aa" and "Aa Aa" text formatting options produce identical results
summary: The reporter expects Aa to perform Sentence Case, while the implementation uses Title Case; the existing Aa and Aa Aa options can therefore look identical on the reported filename.
next_action: Evaluate a distinct Sentence Case option that preserves Title Case, then align the control labels and documentation with all three transformations.

judgment.rationale: The reported lowercase example legitimately produces the same output for Title Case and capitalization of every word because it contains no minor words, but the reporter expects Aa to be Sentence Case. The current implementation is Title Case and the Learn documentation describes Sentence Case. The discussion contains different maintainer preferences about whether to add a distinct option or change the current one; adding a separate Sentence Case operation best addresses the expected behavior without removing Title Case.
evidence: The reporter gave reproducible steps and supplied screenshots showing Aa and Aa Aa produce identical results for the tested filename.
The current PowerRename implementation applies Title Case and has a minor-word exception list, so many inputs correctly produce the same output as Capitalize Every Word.
A maintainer explained that the Aa control currently performs Title Case and confirmed that the Learn documentation describes Sentence Case.
The issue discussion includes a proposal to add a distinct Sentence Case option while retaining Title Case, as well as a different preference about keeping the behavior simple.
judgment.recommended_action: Evaluate adding a distinct Sentence Case operation while preserving Title Case and Capitalize Every Word, then make the UI labels and documentation distinguish all three.

fix_assessment.rationale: The implementation and tests confirm that Aa currently performs Title Case, while the report's expected result is Sentence Case and the documentation uses that terminology. A separate Sentence Case operation can satisfy the expected behavior without changing or removing existing Title Case behavior.

proposed_fixes.title: Add a distinct PowerRename Sentence Case operation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The Aa control applies Title Case, but the reporter expects Sentence Case and the Learn documentation also describes Sentence Case. The current interface therefore has no operation matching the reported expectation, and the Title Case and Capitalize Every Word options can return the same result for filenames without minor words.
plan: Add a separate Sentence Case transformation that uppercases the first alphabetic character of the filename stem and lowercases the remaining stem characters, preserving the extension.
Keep the existing Title Case and Capitalize Every Word transformations unchanged and give all three controls distinct labels and accessible descriptions.
Update the PowerRename text-formatting documentation to describe the three operations and the Title Case minor-word behavior.
Add focused tests for the reported hello world example, a title with a minor word such as lord of the rings, and filenames with extensions.
verification: Verify that Sentence Case produces Hello world, Title Case produces Hello World, and Capitalize Every Word produces Hello World for the reported hello world stem.
Verify that Title Case preserves the configured lowercasing of minor words, while Sentence Case and Capitalize Every Word follow their distinct labels.
Run the focused PowerRename formatting tests and review the published text-formatting documentation.

confidence.rationale: The implementation, tests, and reporter's expected output establish the behavior gap, and a maintainer proposed a separate Sentence Case option. The current maintainer discussion does not yet agree on whether to add a separate control or change the existing one.
